blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Model compression can facilitate the deployment of large language models in resource-constrained legal settings, but its effects on domain-specific performance may depend on the evaluation protocol. We investigate this issue using ArabLegalEval, a Saudi Arabic legal benchmark, under both with-context and no-context evaluation. The former provides supporting legal passages, while the latter assesses performance without external context. Removing the context produces accuracy gaps of up to 27 percentage points for the base model. We examine three stages: domain adaptation, quantization, and knowledge distillation across FANAR-9B, JAIS-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Four-bit quantization reduces model memory by 64-71%, with changes in no-context MCQ accuracy ranging from -3.2 to +1.6 percentage points. Distillation produces more variable results, with accuracy generally declining as student size decreases. A Qwen2.5-7B student distilled from FANAR achieves 76.6% no-context accuracy, compared with 77.2% for its teacher. Our findings suggest that no-context evaluation provides a useful complement to context-supported testing when assessing the effects of adaptation and compression on Arabic legal language models.

promising capabilities in domain-specific
applications, including legal reasoning, contract
analysis, and legal question answering Chalkidis et al. (2020) ; Katz et al. (2023) ; Ariai et al. (2025) .

resources and infrastructure are limited Dong et al. (2025) ; Panjolia et al. (2026) .
Local deployment may help address confidentiality
concerns, although the use of LLMs in legal
applications still requires appropriate human
oversight, jurisdiction-specific validation, and
safeguards against inaccurate legal advice.

blocks.en: 2.1 Arabic LLMs and Legal-Domain Evaluation
blocks.zh: 2.1 阿拉伯法学硕士和法律领域评价

blocks.en:
The Arabic LLM landscape has grown rapidly, progressing from BERT-style encoders to
instruction-tuned generative models such as Jais ( Anwar et al., 2026 ) ,
AceGPT ( Huang et al., 2024 ) , ALLaM ( Bari et al., 2025 ) , and
FANAR ( Team et al., ) . Nevertheless, evaluations of these models in specialized legal
domains remain limited. ArabLegalEval ( Hijazi et al., 2024 ) evaluates Arabic legal
understanding, while MizanQA ( Bahaj and Ghogho, 2026 ) focuses on Moroccan law. Other benchmarks
address related areas, including Islamic inheritance reasoning in QIAS-2026 ( Bouchekif et al., 2026a ) and MAWARITH ( Bouchekif et al., 2026b ) , broader Islamic
knowledge in IslamicMMLU ( Abdelaal et al., 2026 ) , and financial and
Shari’ah-compliant reasoning in SAHM ( Elbadry et al., 2026 ) .

under model compression or how this knowledge should be evaluated when access to source context

studying the effects of adaptation, quantization, and distillation rather than treating benchmark
performance as an endpoint in itself.

blocks.en: 2.2 LLM Compression: Quantization, Distillation, and Adaptation
blocks.zh: 2.2 LLM(低强度) 压缩:量化、稀释和适应

blocks.en:
Post-training quantization methods, including GPTQ ( Frantar et al., 2022 ) ,
AWQ ( Lin et al., 2025 ) , and NF4 ( Dettmers et al., 2023 ) , reduce model size and memory
requirements by lowering weight precision. Knowledge distillation ( Hinton et al., 2015 ) transfers capabilities from a larger teacher to a smaller student, while parameter-efficient
methods such as LoRA ( Hu et al., 2021 ) and QLoRA ( Dettmers et al., 2023 ) support domain
adaptation with limited trainable parameters. Recent studies have examined these approaches
within broader efficiency frameworks ( von Rad et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2024 ) .

blocks.en:
Much of the existing evaluation literature focuses on English or multilingual benchmarks, where the accuracy–size trade-off may differ from morphologically rich, lower-resource languages such as Arabic. Closest to our work, Alshehhi et al. (2025) compress multilingual transformers on Arabic, English, and
Kannada, finding that 4 4 - and 8 8 -bit quantization reduce memory with minimal accuracy loss
on ArabicMMLU ( Koto et al., 2024 ) . We differ in three ways: our domain is Arabic legal understanding; we evaluate adaptation, quantization, and distillation as
three-stage experimental framework on shared models and benchmark; and, most importantly, we
evaluate every stage under both with-context and no-context protocols, which reframes what
“preserved performance” under compression actually means.

blocks.en: For MCQ, models are prompted in Arabic to return a single option label (A–D). We extract the first valid Latin or Arabic option label from the generated response and compute exact-match accuracy. For NajizQA, we report ROUGE-L against the reference answer. Decoding settings are fixed across models and stages, with temperature 0.1 0.1 and top- p p 0.9 0.9 .

blocks.en: 3.4 Stage 2: Post-Training Quantization

blocks.en:
In the second stage, we compress the selected Stage 1 teacher using post-training quantization,
without any additional training. For each base model, the selected CPT → \to SFT adapter is merged
into the base weights to produce a single BF16 checkpoint, which serves as the uncompressed
reference for quantization. (Distillation in Stage 3 instead starts from the SFT checkpoint; see
Section 3.5 .)

floating-point representation. The two 4-bit variants let us compare whether the choice of
low-bit number format affects legal-task performance.

blocks.en: 3.5 Stage 3: Knowledge Distillation
blocks.zh: 3.5 第3阶段:知识消沉

blocks.en: In the third stage, we transfer the teacher’s behavior to smaller student models. Unlike Stage 2, which uses the teacher selected for quantization, distillation uses the Stage 1 SFT checkpoint. We first generate pseudo-labels over the training split. For MCQ items, the teacher is queried in the no-context setting so that the supervision reflects retained legal knowledge rather than direct extraction from the context.
blocks.zh: 在第三阶段,我们把老师的行为转移到较小的学生模式。 与第2阶段使用被选入量化的老师不同的是,蒸馏使用第1阶段SFT检查站. 我们首先在训练课上制造假标签 对于MCQ项目,在无文字的情况下询问教师,以便监督反映保留的法律知识,而不是直接取自背景。

blocks.en: Each student is then fine-tuned on these prompt–response pairs with a standard causal language-modeling objective. This corresponds to sequence-level, hard-label distillation ( Kim and Rush, 2016 ) , where the student learns from the teacher’s generated outputs rather than its full probability distribution. We use this formulation because it is simple and does not require the teacher and student to share the same tokenizer or vocabulary, which also makes cross-family distillation possible. Logit-level distillation with temperature scaling is left for future work.
blocks.zh: 然后,每个学生都会根据这些即时反应对准标准因果语言模型目标进行微调。 这相当于序列级,硬标签分馏(Kim and Rush, 2016),学生从老师产生的出产中学习,而不是完全的概率分布. 我们使用这种配方是因为它很简单,并不要求老师和学生共享相同的标语或词汇,这也使得跨家庭分馏成为可能. 带有温度缩放的逻辑级蒸馏留待未来工作。

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4 实验设置

blocks.en:
We conduct experiments on ArabLegalEval ( Hijazi et al., 2024 ) , focusing on its

training and 2,113 evaluation examples, and

examples. Adaptation and distillation use only
the training data. For evaluation, we use a
fixed subset of 500 held-out MCQ examples and
all 200 NajizQA examples across the relevant
experiments. Further details on MCQ subsampling
are provided in Appendix A.

blocks.en:
We investigated how domain adaptation, quantization,
and knowledge distillation affect Arabic legal MCQ
performance on ArabLegalEval under with-context
and no-context evaluation. The results show that
with-context accuracy is generally high, whereas
no-context performance varies considerably across
models and configurations. This highlights the value
of evaluating models without supporting context when
examining context-independent task performance.

blocks.en: Ethical Consideration
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: This study uses an existing Arabic legal benchmark and publicly available language models, and does not involve human participants or personal data. The compressed models are evaluated for research purposes and are not intended to provide legal advice. As model outputs may contain errors or reflect limitations in the underlying models and benchmark, deployment in real-world legal settings should include appropriate expert oversight and validation.
blocks.zh: 本研究采用现有的阿拉伯语法律基准和可公开使用的语言模型,不涉及人类参与者或个人数据. 对压缩模型进行评价是为了研究目的,而无意提供法律咨询。 由于模型产出可能含有错误或反映了基本模型和基准的局限性,在现实法律环境中的部署应包括适当的专家监督和验证。

blocks.en: We further examined with-context MCQ performance according to whether the correct option text appeared verbatim in the associated legal passage, using the FANAR-9B INT4 NF4 model from Stage 2 (Table 2 ). Of the 500 evaluation examples, 270 (54.0%) contained the correct answer text, while 230 (46.0%) did not. The model answered 268/270 (99.3%) correctly in the former group and 227/230 (98.7%) in the latter, for an overall accuracy of 99.0% (495/500). The small observed difference suggests that exact answer-text overlap alone does not account for the model’s high with-context accuracy. However, this analysis does not distinguish contextual inference from reliance on previously acquired knowledge.
